title: Cannes Opens, Woody Allen Is Much the Same as Ever, and Here's a Guide to the Lineup
excerpt: Which film will be this year's *Carol* or *Mad Max*?
body:
Which film will be this year's *Carol* or *Mad Max*?

With the premiere of *Café Society*, the Cannes Film Festival opened on the 11th. Here is the first thing we learned.

The critical verdict on Woody Allen's third Cannes opening film. To borrow a line from *[The Hollywood Reporter](http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/cafe-society-cannes-review-892693)*'s review: "The same as ever, but still charming."

Over the next week, film fans everywhere will get a lineup that could keep glowing for the rest of the year — the way 2015's *Carol*, *Mad Max: Fury Road*, *Inside Out* and *Son of Saul* stayed in the conversation from May right through to the following year's Oscars.

The 21 films in the main competition will screen one after another, and out of them come the top honors: the Palme d'Or, the acting prizes, the directing prize and the rest. Cannes "regulars" are back — Ken Loach, the Dardenne brothers, Jim Jarmusch, Pedro Almodóvar. Xavier Dolan, Park Chan-wook and Jeff Nichols all bring new films, and each arrives with its own distinct talking point.

Artistic achievement is not the only thing on offer. Hollywood's commercial films also use Cannes to catch the eye of the global market. Steven Spielberg's *The BFG*, screening out of competition, already has a huge billboard up.

This year's Cannes has nothing to do with Chinese cinema. Still, as usual, a few films hope to raise their standing on this international platform. *Battle of Memories*, *Time Raiders* and *Asura* all turn up in the trade magazines inside the market.

Below is QDaily's guide to the Cannes lineup.

## **First, what a few outlets said about *Café Society*, and a joke from the premiere**

*[The Guardian](http://www.theguardian.com/film/2016/may/11/cafe-society-review-woody-allen-kristen-stewart-jesse-eisenberg)*: "Woody Allen's *Café Society* is sweet, sad, fragile and playful, good-looking and charming, and Vittorio Storaro's cinematography is beautiful — but it holds to a pedantic notion of the 'golden age' of 1930s Hollywood and New York."

*[IndieWire](http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/cafe_society_2016/)*: "An anxious Jesse Eisenberg. An expressive Kristen Stewart. In the end, *Café Society* is one more decent — but not great — Allen film."

*[Variety](http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/cafe_society_2016/)*: "This good-looking film leaves you with the feeling that it is all lavish images and never quite becomes a real movie."

**And a joke from the premiere press conference, from Weibo's [@DeepFocus](http://weibo.com/deepfocus?refer_flag=1005055013_):** A woman reporter put a question with a feminist edge to old Woody — "When will you make a love story about a young man falling for an older woman?" He said: "I'd like to, but I have no comparable life experience to draw on."

![Woody Allen and the cast of *Café Society* at the Cannes premiere](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135807e8stqKIrO3PiacEp.jpg-w600)

## Now the main event: the films that could lead this year's awards season

**Loving**

Word is that the Australian actor Joel Edgerton gives a textbook performance here.

In recent years Jeff Nichols has been the American writer-director most warmly received by the European festivals. His 2011 film *Take Shelter* won the Critics' Week Grand Prize at the 64th Cannes, and *Mud*, from 2012, starring Matthew McConaughey, also made the main competition. Earlier this year, in fact, another fine Nichols film, the science-fiction *Midnight Special*, was selected for competition in Berlin — two of his films at Europe's three big festivals in a single year.

The story is drawn from the real experience of an interracial American couple in the 1950s and '60s.

![A still from *Loving*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135808laZngcuQTrI25pMK.jpg-w600)

**It's Only the End of the World**

Xavier Dolan — 27 years old, Canadian, an actor, writer, director and producer — has talent, looks, and a nickname any filmmaker would envy: "Cannes's own son." Ever since *I Killed My Mother*, his 2009 directing debut, nearly every film he has made has drawn attention at Cannes. *Mommy*, from 2014, won the Jury Prize.

The new film has an all-star cast: the Oscar-winning Marion Cotillard, Léa Seydoux of *Blue Is the Warmest Colour*, and the French leading man Vincent Cassel. A gay writer comes home after 12 years away to tell his family he has AIDS.

Cotillard is again a strong contender for Best Actress.

![A still from *It's Only the End of the World*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135808lBymC8JqMQwZYIvW.jpg-w600)

**Personal Shopper**

The French director Olivier Assayas has reached the Cannes main competition four times before, with *Cold Water*, *Sentimental Destinies*, *Demonlover* and *Clean*. *Clean* won its star, Maggie Cheung — to whom he was once married — the Best Actress prize at Cannes.

The film is about the dark side of the Paris fashion world. The lead is once again Kristen Stewart, the "Twilight girl," and she is in every single shot.

She has become one of the French public's favorite American actors in recent years, winning the César for Best Supporting Actress in 2014 for Assayas's *Clouds of Sils Maria*.

![A still from *Personal Shopper*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135809O6rQZCN4mR83hyFd.jpg-w600)

**The Last Face**

Directed by Sean Penn, starring the Oscar-winning Charlize Theron and the Spanish actor Javier Bardem. *Mad Max: Fury Road*, which Theron carried last year, set the whole critical world talking after its Cannes premiere, so this film could easily become an awards-season favorite too. It is about people in a refugee camp in Sudan, Africa.

Penn and Theron, incidentally, made their relationship public around the time the film went into production. They have since split up.

![A still from *The Last Face*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135809dtDel63r7sXwkqJf.jpg-w600)

**Elle**

The Dutch director Paul Verhoeven is best known for the erotic classic *Basic Instinct*. This time he works with the French actress Isabelle Huppert, returning to the thriller he does so well and to the themes of sex and violence.

Michèle, a hard-driving businesswoman, is raped by a masked man in her own home; she then works her way through the men around her to find out who the attacker really was.

![A still from *Elle*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135810uMC9TLAOI3ZPUg7N.jpg-w600)

**Julieta**

The 20th film by the great Spanish director Pedro Almodóvar. *All About My Mother* won him Best Director at Cannes in 1999, and *Volver* took Best Screenplay and Best Actress in 2006.

After *I'm So Excited!* failed with critics in 2013, Almodóvar returns to women's stories. Two actresses share the title role: Adriana Ugarte plays her in her thirties, Emma Suárez at 50.

![A still from *Julieta*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201607021358110fIoWlN9M4ejx6qK.jpg-w600)

**The Salesman**

The Iranian director Asghar Farhadi stunned the film world in 2011 with *A Separation*.

His 2013 film *The Past* won its lead, Bérénice Bejo, the Best Actress prize at Cannes. *The Salesman* follows a young Tehran couple who move house and are pulled into trouble left behind by the previous tenant.

![A still from *The Salesman*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135811YBwPfUC8QdDOZ7kH.jpg-w600)

**The Unknown Girl**

Another pair of filmmaking brothers: Luc Dardenne and Jean-Pierre Dardenne, who also made their name through Cannes. *The Kid with a Bike* won the Cannes Grand Prix in 2011, and Marion Cotillard, the lead of *Two Days, One Night*, from 2014, was nominated for an Oscar.

A young doctor, Jenny, finds a girl's body near her clinic.

Its lead, Adèle Haenel, is one of the serious French actors who have broken through in recent years.

![A still from *The Unknown Girl*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201607021358126duSXrRVz1Ypj375.jpg-w600)

**American Honey**

The British director Andrea Arnold is in the Cannes main competition for the third time. *Red Road* won the Jury Prize at Cannes in 2006. She has also directed episodes of *Transparent*, Amazon's much-praised series.

A teenage girl crosses the American Midwest with a group of wildly different characters.

![A still from *American Honey*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135812UEcwtM2ObPnLAQTa.jpg-w600)

**The Neon Demon**

The Danish director Nicolas Winding Refn works at the extreme end of taste. *Drive* won him Best Director at Cannes in 2011, but *Only God Forgives* split the festival in 2013.

*The Neon Demon* is about a young girl who comes to Los Angeles hoping to become a model. Her innocence and eagerness bring her great success, and stir up envy and greed in the people around her. Elle Fanning plays the lead.

![A still from *The Neon Demon*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135813qk2PDXZR9TJWVvfI.jpg-w600)

**The Handmaiden**

The South Korean director Park Chan-wook's "fondness" for cruelty and bloody violence has made him a favorite with audiences who like strong stuff, and a regular at the European festivals.

The script comes from *Fingersmith*, the 2002 novel by the British lesbian writer Sarah Waters. Set in the 1930s, it is the story of the love between a noblewoman who has inherited a large fortune and the maid who means her no good.

![A still from *The Handmaiden*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135813H8up3rXSwAdz6xfo.jpg-w600)

**Paterson**

The American independent filmmaker Jim Jarmusch is competing in the Cannes main competition for the eighth time. His best-known films — *Down by Law*, *Mystery Train*, *Dead Man*, *Broken Flowers*, *Night on Earth* — make cool, estranged images on small budgets.

*Paterson* is about a bus driver who is secretly a hermit poet.

![A still from *Paterson*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135814J3glSkNmhKaUnAzI.jpg-w600)

## **Hollywood out of competition, with Spielberg in the spotlight again**

**The BFG (Out of Competition)**

Produced by Disney, Steven Spielberg's new film comes from the British children's book: a "Big Friendly Giant" who likes collecting good dreams and a little girl named Sophie set out to stop the other giants from eating people.

Ruby Barnhill, a 10-year-old child actor, plays Sophie. Mark Rylance, who won Best Supporting Actor at the 88th Academy Awards last year for *Bridge of Spies*, plays the Giant. It opens in the United States on July 1; a Chinese release has not been confirmed.

![A still from *The BFG*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135814mCArPFSQ5dfUGWxO.jpg-w600)

**The Nice Guys (Out of Competition)**

Its Chinese title, 《耐撕侦探》, puns on "nice" and is pleasingly down to earth. A gangster comedy from Warner Bros., with two leads, Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling, directed by Shane Black of *Iron Man 3*. It opens in North America on May 20.

Los Angeles, 1970: a mob enforcer and a private detective are thrown together by the apparent suicide of an adult-film actress.

![A still from *The Nice Guys*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201607021358154Y6JprSl9LXVMwWQ.jpg-w600)

**Money Monster (Out of Competition)**

Jodie Foster's new film as a director, a suspense thriller with an A-list cast: George Clooney, Julia Roberts, Jack O'Connell. It opens on May 13.

The plot resembles *The Terror Live*. A pundit on a TV finance show has made a Wall Street fortune on insider tips; one of his viewers, who followed his on-air advice and lost everything, kidnaps him in a rage. The whole thing goes out live on television, and everyone wants to see what a person's life is worth.

![A still from *Money Monster*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135815PqIwWmRHzY9S7FTQ.jpg-w600)

## Two more films, from Japan and South Korea, both by directors we like

*After the Storm* (Un Certain Regard)

*Our Little Sister* was the Japanese film Chinese audiences liked best last year. Its director, Hirokazu Kore-eda, is very good on the pull of family.

*After the Storm* takes as its theme "people caught between life and their ideals." An old woman living alone, her son, the son's ex-wife and her grandson are forced back together by a typhoon. Hiroshi Abe plays the son, a writer whose day has passed.

![A still from *After the Storm*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135816uRq1kVIJ0Fo6ZlGn.jpg-w600)

**The Wailing (Out of Competition)**

Two strong films, *The Chaser* (2008) and *The Yellow Sea* (2010), made Na Hong-jin one of the best-known South Korean filmmakers abroad.

In *The Wailing*, strange things start happening in a village in Gokseong County, South Jeolla Province, after an eerie Japanese man arrives. The detective sent to investigate believes in scientific method and is left with nothing to go on in the face of the strangeness; a shaman joins him in trying to get to the bottom of it.

![A still from *The Wailing*](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135817Lvpz7OasMDdAkUox.jpg-w600)

## Finally, no Chinese film made the selection, but you will still see familiar faces

**The trade dailies**

*Battle of Memories*, the New Year holiday film with Huang Bo and Xu Jinglei, made the cover of *Screen*, the festival's day-one daily. *Asura*, the fantasy film from Ningxia Film Group, unveiled its "Union of Heaven and Earth" poster on the cover of *Variety*'s festival special issue.

Inside: Jackie Chan's new films *Kung Fu Yoga*, *Railroad Tigers* and *Deadly Countdown* (《致命倒数》); Ann Hui's new film *Our Time Will Come*; Universe Entertainment's *Call of Heroes* and *Shock Wave*; and *Time Raiders*, with Jing Boran and Lu Han.

![The cover of the Cannes day-one trade daily](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135817snb6xmNJtec9a0wG.jpg-w600)

![A page of Chinese film ads inside the festival trade magazine](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135817xmFp6XHEtsu0wYiy.jpg-w600)

**Little Door Gods**

Light Chaser Animation announced a formal partnership with The Weinstein Company, handing it the overseas distribution rights to *Little Door Gods*, the studio's first animated feature. The English-language version's voice cast is confirmed: Meryl Streep, Nicole Kidman, Zendaya and Mel Brooks.

**Time Raiders**

Jing Boran, Ma Sichun and Nanpai Sanshu, the author of the novel, went to Cannes. A scheduling mistake by the publicity team meant they never made it onto the red carpet…

![The *Time Raiders* team at Cannes](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135818TEyMH8zd3x501mvn.jpg-w600)

![The *Time Raiders* team at Cannes](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160702135819P96ae2qIbnVHJGQ7.jpg-w600)
